validity.recommendation: Retire or move this row off GGIT (the gas tracker) — every independent source describes the Rattlesnake Extension as a crude-oil (and produced-water/freshwater) gathering/transportation line, not gas transmission. This is the same classification defect batch 4 flagged on the parent system row P0386 (Pipeline News Oct-2018, Rigzone Jun-2020, OGJ Sep-2019, energyspectrum.com all describe crude-oil/water gathering, gas at most minor). Do not research it further as an oil line — oil is out of scope this cycle — but the row itself belongs on GOIT, not GGIT, or should carry a note that it is erroneously in the gas tracker.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's own Fuel value ('Oil') is CORRECT and independently confirmed — the anomaly is that a crude-oil row sits on the GAS infrastructure tracker (GGIT) at all. Businesswire press release (Sept 16, 2019, archived via Wayback since live fetch 403s bots) and OGJ's write-up of it (Sept 17, 2019, live) both state Taproot Rockies Midstream 'secured a long-term acreage dedication for CRUDE OIL transportation from Bonanza Creek Energy' and will extend its Baja System 'approximately 35 miles south (the Rattlesnake Extension) to transport Bonanza Creek's crude oil ... for re-delivery at Tallgrass Energy Partners' Buckingham Terminal ... with ultimate delivery to Cushing,' explicitly for 'Niobrara-spec crude oil barrels.' Rigzone (June 2, 2020), reporting a separate Mallard Exploration acreage deal, states 'Taproot's existing Baja System and soon-to-be-completed Rattlesnake expansion include over 110 miles of OIL, PRODUCED WATER and FRESHWATER pipelines' — no gas is mentioned anywhere in any of the three articles. I also checked EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (both the current-projects and 1996-2024 historical-projects tabs, downloaded live 2026-09-10): it has no Taproot/Rattlesnake/Baja entry at all — the only 'Baja' hits are the unrelated Sempra/TC Energy 'North Baja Pipeline' (Arizona-to-Mexico gas line), which is expected if Taproot's system carries no gas. This corroborates batch 4's P0386 finding rather than contradicting it — P2041 is the Rattlesnake Extension SEGMENT of that same system, correctly linked (kind=cluster, pipeline_name=Taproot Baja Pipeline System), not a duplicate of P0386, but it inherits the same tracker-placement problem.

validity.recommendation: Do not paste Owner1='Energy Spectrum Securities' as confirmed. Verify the exact legal fund entity before treating it as sourced; consider 'Energy Spectrum Capital' pending a document that names the specific holding vehicle.
validity.researcher_notes: Same open question batch 4 flagged on P0386 (Owner 'Energy Spectrum Securities' vs the firm's own 'Energy Spectrum Capital'), and it does not resolve cleanly. The Sept 2019 Businesswire press release — Taproot's own announcement, the most authoritative source available — states twice that 'Taproot is backed by ENERGY SPECTRUM CAPITAL, based in Dallas, Texas' and gives an 'About Energy Spectrum Capital' boilerplate; it never uses the string 'Energy Spectrum Securities.' SEC EDGAR (checked live with a declared UA per the ladder) DOES list a real, distinct registered entity named 'Energy Spectrum Securities Corp,' alongside half a dozen separate 'Energy Spectrum Capital/Partners' fund LPs (Capital IV LP, Capital VI LP, Partners IV-VIII LP) — so 'Energy Spectrum Securities' is not a typo for a nonexistent name, but no document I found ties that specific Securities Corp entity (as opposed to one of the Capital/Partners funds) to Taproot Rockies Midstream or Taproot Energy Partners. Given the sponsor's own press materials consistently self-identify as 'Energy Spectrum Capital,' the sheet's Owner1 value is more likely wrong than right, but I can't name the exact correct fund-level entity from what I found — flagging rather than silently changing it. Cross-ref: P0386 (batch 4), same open item.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is not the proposed/shelved dormancy case the 2y/4y rules address — it's an already-operating row with a blank LastUpdated. I hunted for dated evidence: OGJ (Sept 2019) — agreement executed, Q2-2020 in-service target; Rigzone (June 2020) — 'soon-to-be-completed Rattlesnake expansion,' no hint of trouble; a Civitas Resources 8-K exhibit (SEC EDGAR, filed March 2, 2022, for an unrelated Bison Oil & Gas asset acquisition in the same DJ Basin footprint) explicitly names 'Taproot Rockies Midstream, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company' as a still-extant, non-affiliated counterparty — proof the entity was a going concern nearly 3 years after the extension was announced. I searched further for a direct 2023-2026 'currently operating' statement (SEC EDGAR full-text search for 'Taproot,' Bing/DuckDuckGo via curl — WebSearch tool budget was exhausted for this session — PHMSA/NPMS map viewer, which is JS-rendered and not scriptable) and found nothing more recent or contradictory. No evidence anywhere of cancellation, idling, sale of the pipeline asset itself, or abandonment. On that basis I'm confirming 'operating' rather than flagging staleness, at medium tier because the newest direct evidence (2022) proves continued corporate existence rather than literally 'still moving oil today.'

summary: P2041 (Taproot Rattlesnake Extension) is real and well-corroborated (OGJ 2019, Rigzone 2020, SEC/Civitas 8-K 2022) but is a crude-oil/produced-water gathering line, not gas — filed as a classification concern (same issue batch 4 raised on parent P0386) plus an attribution concern on Owner1 ('Energy Spectrum Securities' vs the sponsor's own 'Energy Spectrum Capital'); Length 35 mi and Operator confirmed at REFS_ADDED, Status/Fuel/Proposal/Start/Location confirmed at REFS_ADDED with caveats noted.
